sftr_securities_finance_report.text: `emir_clearing_obligation_check` answers whether a counterparty falls under EMIR's clearing obligation, while `sftr_securities_finance_report` answers whether a securities financing transaction report has its core fields filled in correctly. The first takes `notionals`, `counterparty_category` ("FC", "NFC+" or "NFC-") and `clearing_thresholds`, and compares each asset class's notional with its threshold. For an FC, breaching in any one asset class puts all its asset classes under clearing. For an NFC+, only the classes it breaches are affected. The second takes a single `transaction` mapping and validates a core subset of SFTR fields for repos, securities lending, buy-sell backs and margin lending, such as counterparties, UTI, collateral and the SFT type. So one is a regulatory scope test on derivatives positions, and the other is a field-presence and format check on a transaction report.

explain.text: `emir_clearing_obligation_check` (EMIR Clearing Obligation Check) works out which OTC derivative asset classes a counterparty must clear under EMIR REFIT. You give it `notionals` per asset class, a `counterparty_category` ("FC", "NFC+" or "NFC-"), and `clearing_thresholds` per asset class. For a Financial Counterparty, breaching the threshold in any one class brings all the classes it holds positions in under the obligation. For an NFC+, each class is judged separately, so only classes where its own threshold is breached are caught. pyvar does the comparison; the citation is Art. 4a(1) / Art. 10(1).

issues: Says NFC- is a valid input but not what the function does for it (exempt).
Bullet on reviewing an earlier per-class approach is an odd use case.

when.text:
Use the EMIR Clearing Obligation Check (`emir_clearing_obligation_check`) when you need to see which OTC derivative asset classes fall under EMIR clearing for a given counterparty:

- You know the counterparty is a Financial Counterparty (`"FC"`) and want to see whether a breach in any one asset class pulls all its asset classes into clearing.
- The counterparty is a Non-Financial Counterparty above threshold (`"NFC+"`), and you want each asset class judged on its own threshold.
- You hold gross notionals for every asset class the counterparty trades, plus a clearing threshold for each, and want to pass them in as `notionals` and `clearing_thresholds`.
- You're reviewing an earlier per-class-only approach for FCs, which could understate the clearing scope.

If the counterparty is `"NFC-"`, it is also a valid `counterparty_category` input.

For a different need, `emir_margin_requirement` covers the EMIR (Art. 11) uncleared-derivatives margin requirement.
